questions.q: Write the equation of a circle with center $(-4,7)$ and radius $9$.
The circle below has the radius shown. Find its area and circumference, in terms of $\pi$.
A circle has diameter $26$ and is centered at the origin. Write its equation, and state its radius.
Find the center and radius of $x^2+y^2-6x+8y-11=0$.
Find the center and radius of $x^2+y^2+10x-4y+13=0$.
Find the distance between $(-3,5)$ and $(4,-7)$, to the nearest hundredth.
Find the midpoint and slope of the segment joining $(2,-6)$ and $(-8,10)$.
Find the slope of the line through $(-2,7)$ and $(6,-5)$, and state whether the line rises or falls from left to right.
questions.answer: Slope $=\dfrac{-5-7}{6-(-2)}=\dfrac{-12}{8}=-\dfrac{3}{2}$. Since the slope is negative, the line falls from left to right.

questions.q: Show that the triangle with vertices $A(0,0)$, $B(4,0)$, $C(4,3)$ is a right triangle, using slopes.
questions.answer: Slope of $AB=\dfrac{0-0}{4-0}=0$ (horizontal). Slope of $BC$ is undefined (vertical, since $x=4$ for both points). A horizontal segment and a vertical segment are perpendicular, so $\angle B=90^\circ$, confirming a right triangle.

questions.q: Show that $A(1,2)$, $B(4,3)$, $C(3,6)$, $D(0,5)$ form a parallelogram, by showing both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
questions.answer: Slope $AB=\dfrac{3-2}{4-1}=\dfrac{1}{3}$. Slope $DC=\dfrac{6-5}{3-0}=\dfrac{1}{3}$, so $AB\parallel DC$. Slope $AD=\dfrac{5-2}{0-1}=-3$. Slope $BC=\dfrac{6-3}{3-4}=-3$, so $AD\parallel BC$. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

questions.q: A circle has center $O(2,3)$ and radius $5$. Point $P(2,12)$ lies outside the circle. Find the length of the tangent from $P$ to the circle, to the nearest hundredth.
Find the equation of the tangent line to the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ at the point $(3,4)$ on the circle.
questions.answer: The radius to $(3,4)$ has slope $\dfrac{4}{3}$, so the tangent (perpendicular to the radius) has slope $-\dfrac{3}{4}$. Line: $y-4=-\dfrac{3}{4}(x-3)$, which simplifies to $3x+4y=25$.

questions.q: A circle has center $(0,0)$ and radius $10$. Determine whether the point $(6,9)$ lies inside, on, or outside the circle.
questions.answer: Distance from center $=\sqrt{6^2+9^2}=\sqrt{117}\approx10.82$, which is greater than the radius $10$. The point lies outside the circle.

questions.q: A central angle of $84^\circ$ subtends an arc. Find the measure of the inscribed angle subtending the same arc.
A chord subtends the central angle shown below. Find the measure of the inscribed angle subtending the same (minor) arc.
A circle has radius $12$ cm. Find the arc length subtended by a central angle of $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ radians.
The circle below has the radius and shaded sector shown. Find the area of the sector, in terms of $\pi$.
A sector of a circle with radius $9$ has area $27\pi$. Find the central angle, in radians.
Identify the type of conic and state its center for $\dfrac{(x-2)^2}{16}+\dfrac{(y+1)^2}{9}=1$.
questions.answer: An ellipse, centered at $(2,-1)$, with $a^2=16$ ($a=4$, horizontal major axis) and $b^2=9$ ($b=3$).

questions.q: Identify the type of conic, its center, and its asymptote slopes for $\dfrac{(x+3)^2}{4}-\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$.
questions.answer: A hyperbola, centered at $(-3,0)$, with $a=2$, $b=3$. Asymptote slopes: $\pm\dfrac{b}{a}=\pm\dfrac{3}{2}$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a Ferris wheel

questions.q: This question has three parts. A circular Ferris wheel has a diameter of $40$ m, with its center $22$ m above the ground. Set up a coordinate system with the origin at ground level, directly below the center. (a) Write the equation of the circle traced by a passenger cabin. (b) A support cable runs from a ground anchor at $(26,0)$ to a point of tangency on the wheel. Find the length of this cable, to the nearest hundredth of a meter. (c) Find the height above the ground of a cabin when it is $12$ m horizontally from the vertical line through the center.
questions.answer: (a) Center $(0,22)$, radius $20$: $x^2+(y-22)^2=400$. (b) $OP=\sqrt{26^2+22^2}=\sqrt{1160}\approx34.06$ m. Tangent length $=\sqrt{OP^2-r^2}=\sqrt{1160-400}=\sqrt{760}\approx27.57$ m. (c) With $x=12$: $12^2+(y-22)^2=400\Rightarrow(y-22)^2=256\Rightarrow y=22\pm16$, so $y=38$ m or $y=6$ m.
